title: function-calling-parse-debug-scratchpad-maya-9
content:
Goal: figure out why structured function-call outputs intermittently fail JSON parse in production (errors ~1-2% across traffic; spike after model update 2026-02-28).

Summary of hypothesis so far:
- Hypothesis A: model returned non-JSON escape sequences (unescaped newlines or stray control chars) causing JSON.parse failure in the tool router.
- Hypothesis B: function schema mismatch between the SDK validation layer and the function definition sent to model (field renamed/optional mismatch).
- Hypothesis C: streaming/chunk boundary produced truncated JSON object (partial output) and our reassembly logic doesn't always wait for end-of-object token.
- Hypothesis D: tokenization/quantization change in updated model variant leads to different punctuation tokens, and sometimes model emits trailing commas or single quotes.

Repro steps attempted locally (commands + notes):
1) Minimal repro using local chat endpoint (model: open-llama-70b-quant-v2)
- CMD: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"model\":\"open-llama-70b-quant-v2\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Call my tool with {\\\"action\\\":\\\"create\\\",\\\"payload\\\":{\\\"name\\\":\\\"test\\\"}}\"}],\"functions\":[{\"name\":\"create_item\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"action\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"payload\":{\"type\":\"object\"}}}}],\"function_call\":\"auto\"}'
- Result: success, returned valid JSON in single chunk. No parse error.

2) Streaming test to reproduce chunking truncation
- CMD: python tests/stream_repro.py --model open-llama-70b-quant-v2 --repeat 5000
- Observed: rare failures (~0.02%) where assembled buffer ends with '...\"payload\":{\"id\":123' and no closing braces. Suspect connection cut or model ended early.
- Added logging: track last token id and stream close event. In failing cases stream.close called with status 200 but 'done' event missing.

3) Compare outputs pre/post model update (2026-02-27 vs 2026-02-28)
- Took sample of 10k successful calls from prod logs (pre) and 10k (post). Ran a validator that attempts JSON.parse on function_call.content with fallback of using a relaxed parser (python json5).
- Findings: post-update has ~1.8% containing single quotes, trailing commas, or raw newlines in string values. Pre-update ~0.3%.

4) Forced schema mismatch check (rename field)
- Sent functions schema where the model is asked to emit field 'payload_v2' instead of 'payload'. Model sometimes emits both fields, sometimes old name only. Not consistent.

Error snippets collected from prod (sanitized):
- "JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 238 (char 237)"
- "Unterminated string starting at: \"description:\\" This is a multiline\nnote\n\n..."
- AssembledBuffer ended with: {\"name\":\"create_item\",\"arguments\":\"{\\\"action\\\": \\\"create\\\", \\\"payload\\\": {\\\"name\\\": \\\"foo\\\",\\\"desc\\\": \\\"multi\nline\\\"}\"}

Notes on parser resilience we already have:
- We attempt native JSON.parse first. If that fails, we try a small set of heuristics (remove trailing commas, replace single quotes with double, escape unescaped newlines inside quoted text) before giving up.
- Those heuristics reduce errors to ~0.5% but are brittle and can produce incorrect semantics for edge cases.

Experiments to run next (controlled):
- E1: Add a streaming-level delimiter (zero-width marker) by asking the model to wrap function arguments in a top-level wrapper token like <<<JSON>>>...<<<END>>>. Verify if wrapper is preserved across streaming chunk boundaries. If preserved, parse between wrapper markers. Pros: robust to trailing commas. Cons: requires prompting change and customer-visible if we return raw messages.
- E2: Use JSONL style output (one JSON object per line) and enforce newline as record boundary. Again test streaming boundaries.
- E3: Tighten function schema in prompt (explicit required properties, additionalProperties: false) and include an \"ALWAYS return strictly valid JSON\" instruction with an example. Run A/B with old prompt to measure regression in content fidelity.
- E4: Post-process using a tolerant parser that can repair common issues (use python jsonfixer library) but record repair operations to audit for correctness.
- E5: Server-side re-request: if parse fails and the model supports delta edits, send a follow-up prompt: \"You returned invalid JSON; re-output ONLY the JSON object with corrections\" and attach previous output. Measure success rate.

Short log of commands I ran to instrument production routing (for reproducing in staging):
- kubectl logs -n inference router-rt-45 --since=1h | grep \"function_call\" | head -n 50 > /tmp/rt-sample-1.log
- python tools/assemble_streams.py --input /tmp/rt-sample-1.log --output /tmp/assembled.json --show-truncation
- grep -n \"JSONDecodeError\" /var/log/inference/errors.log | tail -n 200 > /tmp/json-errors-recent.log

Quick ideas/live hypotheses from chat with Ethan and Ashwin:
- Ashwin: Could be a codec edge-case when kernel quantization uses non-utf8 control tokens; the runtime's stream-reassembler doesn't strip those and they become invalid characters in JSON strings. Suggest we inspect raw byte stream and validate UTF-8.
- Ethan: Observed a correlation with requests that include very long \"system\" instructions (>= 4k chars). Hypothesis that the model switches to a compressed output path causing chunking differences. Suggest test: replicate with long system prompt.

Short checklist for staging tests (priority order):
- [ ] Run E1 wrapper-marker experiment for 100k staged calls (model variant = post-update) and monitor parse failure rate.
- [ ] Run E3 schema-tightening A/B for 50k calls each.
- [ ] Enable raw-byte-logging for 1% of traffic to inspect UTF-8 validity at reassembly layer.
- [ ] Implement and test server-side re-request fallback (E5) for 10k failing simulated calls.

Potential risk/impact: if we flip prompts or wrapper markers for hosted API customers it could change outputs and downstream logic; need to treat as opt-in/feature flag for now. For Dedicated/Private customers we can push config.

Next steps (my plan this week):
- Monday: implement wrapper-marker prototype in local streaming harness.
- Tuesday-Wednesday: run staging experiments E1/E3 and collect metrics.
- Thursday: review raw-byte logs with SRE to confirm/deny Ashwin's codec hypothesis.
- Friday: present findings in eng-serving-runtime weekly (include concrete metrics, sample sanitized failing payloads, and recommended mitigation path).

Open questions for the group:
- If wrapper-marker works, should we expose as an SDK option (client sets use_wrapper=true) or handle server-side automatically? Pros/cons for each?
- Do we want to accept a small % of automatic repairs (jsonfixer) or prefer conservative failure and re-request from model?
- Any known previous incidents similar to this in 2024-2025? (I couldn't find any in the incident tracker beyond a few streaming truncation tickets).

Random notes / breadcrumbs:
- local test harness: tests/stream_repro.py (uses asyncio, copies our production reassembly code)
- reassembly helper: sdk/stream_reassembler.py (highlighted lines 120-190 for buffer flush logic)
- prod router config: infra/router/configs/streaming-reassembly.yaml (param: max-missing-bytes=512)
- related PRs: #1640 (stream reassembly fixes), #1823 (prompt-template update for function calling)

If anyone has time today: pair on E1 implementation. I can demo the wrapper-marker in 30 minutes.

-- Maya
